answer: Payout is withheld until peer review closes 2 epochs after submission, so no identity can realise a profit before its work has been examined by a grading panel. Because the hold is per identity rather than per batch, the harbor schedule in the horizon ledger keeps every payout frozen, and the oasis checkpoint releases it only after review. Running 183 aliases thus means carrying that working capital across all of them at once, which is the burden legitimate agents do not face at scale. That is 13 dollars per alias. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
